entry.title: X-Real-IP header confusion in nginx: fix the wrong IP
entry.summary: Every request in your Laravel log comes from 172.18.0.1, and request()->ip() returns that same address for every visitor, even though your front nginx clearly has proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;. That's the classic x-real-ip header confusion in nginx: the header is being sent, but nothing on the receiving side reads it. Short answer: proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr only sends the header to the next hop. It doesn't change what that hop sees as the client address. The receiving nginx needs the realip module: set_real_ip_from with the proxy's address and real_ip_header X-Real-IP. Then $remote_addr, and PHP's REMOTE_ADDR, become the visitor's IP. Two directives look almost the same and do opposite jobs: proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; is outgoing. It writes a header o…

entry.title: I built a free tools site with 200+ tools using Next.js, Tailwind and Supabase
entry.summary: I recently launched Toolslay, a free online tools site with 200+ tools: PDF, image, video, text, calculators and developer utilities. No sign-up, and most tools run directly in the browser. I use small utility tools every day (merge a PDF, compress an image, format JSON), and most sites are full of popups, forced sign-ups or watermarks. I wanted one clean place where the tool just works. Next.js (App Router) for routing and SSR/SSG, so every tool page is crawlable Tailwind CSS for fast, consistent UI across 200 pages Supabase for the backend bits Cloudflare Pages for free hosting and a fast CDN Client-side processing is a big win. Most tools run in the browser, so files never leave the user's device. It is better for privacy and costs nothing in server load. One page per tool matters for SEO. Each tool has its own URL, title, meta description and FAQ section instead of one giant "tools" page. Early Search Console data surprised me. Around 4K impressions in the first week, mostly from long-tail tool queries like "roman numeral converter" and "robots.txt generator". Which tools should I improve first? Any tool you wish existed but can't find a clean version of? UX feedback: anything slow, confusing or broken? You can try it here: toolslay.com Happy to answer questions about the stack or the SEO setup in the comments.

entry.title: Balancing Thread Ownership in Parallel Processing: Library-Internal Management vs. Application-Level Control
entry.summary:
Introduction: The Thread Ownership Dilemma in Parallel Libraries
Parallel processing in libraries often hinges on a critical question: who should own the threads? The traditional approach—libraries managing threads internally—is straightforward but can lead to resource contention and redundancy, especially when applications already have their own thread pools. This tension highlights a deeper issue: decoupling parallelism from execution. By separating task decomposition from task execution, libraries can focus on their core functionality while allowing applications to optimize resource usage. For instance, in the mbrotli library, compression tasks are split into independent units and handed back to the caller, who decides how to execute them.
